pattern_description: Fraudsters build romantic or friendly trust online (via dating apps, social media, or random text misdirects), then slowly manipulate the victim into investing in fraudulent crypto trading platforms or high-yield liquidity pools where initial small returns are shown, but total funds are eventually locked and unrecoverable.
example_text: Hey babe, my uncle is an insider at a major crypto exchange. We can make a guaranteed 20% return on this liquidity pool tonight. Log into our private portal and deposit USDT to start.
red_flags: Guaranteed high returns on crypto or forex trading
Met online or via accidental wrong-number text, moving quickly to financial topics
Proprietary or unknown trading platform/app sideloaded outside official app stores
Inability to withdraw funds without paying extra 'taxes' or 'gas fees'
source_citation: INTERPOL Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment & FBI IC3 Advisory on Crypto-Investment Fraud
legit_contrast: Regulated financial institutions and legitimate brokers never guarantee investment returns, nor do they force deposits via unverified crypto wallets or obscure web apps.

pattern_description: Cybercriminals compromise corporate email accounts or use domain spoofing to impersonate C-level executives, directors, or trusted foreign vendors, urgently instructing finance staff to redirect an upcoming wire transfer or invoice payment to a new overseas beneficiary account.
example_text: Urgent wire transfer required for our confidential acquisition in Europe today. Bypass normal audit procedures and send the €250,000 to our new intermediary bank account immediately.
red_flags: Request to bypass internal dual-control or verification protocols
Sudden change of beneficiary bank details or international routing numbers
Urgent tone and creation of artificial time pressure by company executives
Subtle domain spoofing (e.g., changing one letter in a corporate email domain)
source_citation: Europol IOCTA & Financial Crime Enforcement Network (FinCEN) Advisory on BEC
legit_contrast: Legitimate enterprise accounting policies strictly require multi-party verification, callback confirmation, and formal change-of-banking documentation before altering payment vectors.

pattern_description: Victims receive automated SMS or email alerts claiming an international parcel is stuck at a customs checkpoint or courier warehouse, demanding a nominal clearance fee or digital signature through a malicious link that harvests credit card credentials.
example_text: Your international package is on hold at customs due to unpaid import duties of $3.50 USD. Pay immediately to avoid return-to-sender: https://dhl-express-tracking-update.co/fee
red_flags: Unsolicited messages with suspicious non-official short links or mismatched TLDs (.co, .xyz)
A minor fee requested to clear a major package
Creating immediate panic regarding shipment cancellation or return
Lack of authentic tracking number recognized on official logistics registries
source_citation: Global Anti-Scam Alliance (GASA) & Universal Postal Union Cybersecurity Warning
legit_contrast: Major global couriers (DHL, FedEx, UPS) and postal services do not request credit card details via random SMS links for customs duties prior to official physical processing.

pattern_description: An online partner whom the victim has never met in person claims to be traveling, working abroad, or facing sudden medical/legal custody emergencies, requesting urgent money transfers via wire services, gift cards, or cryptocurrency.
example_text: Darling, my passport and wallet were stolen at the airport in London. I am stuck at the terminal and the airline won't let me board. Please wire $1,500 via Western Union right now.
red_flags: Relationship established entirely online without a single face-to-face meeting or video call
Sudden catastrophic emergency requiring immediate financial assistance
Demand for unconventional payment methods (cryptocurrency, gift cards, wire transfers)
Inconsistent stories or refusal to verify identity via local authorities
source_citation: US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Consumer Protection Advisory on Romance Scams
legit_contrast: Legitimate personal relationships do not rely on urgent, unverified cross-border financial wire transfers to resolve sudden travel or medical crises.

pattern_description: Scammers pose as technical staff from global tech giants (Microsoft, Apple, major banks) claiming the victim's computer or bank account has been hacked, tricking them into installing remote-access software to steal credentials or execute bank transfers.
example_text: Critical security alert from Microsoft: Your device is infected with malicious ransomware. Download AnyDesk immediately so our certified technician can secure your bank accounts.
red_flags: Unsolicited pop-ups or phone calls claiming severe malware infections
Instructions to download remote desktop software (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk)
Demands to log into online banking while under remote observation
Fear-inducing language warning of total asset loss or legal liability
source_citation: Interpol Cybercrime Directorate & Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) Alerts
legit_contrast: Genuine software and cloud providers never monitor individual consumer desktop security errors dynamically via cold calls or require remote access utilities to fix system issues.

category: Global Tax Authority / Government Impersonation Scam
pattern_description: Fraudsters impersonate national tax agencies (e.g., IRS in the US, HMRC in the UK, CRA in Canada) or law enforcement via robocalls or emails, threatening immediate arrest, asset seizure, or deportation unless an immediate fine is settled.
example_text: This is final notice from the Internal Revenue Service. A federal arrest warrant has been issued under your name for tax evasion. Press 1 immediately to settle your balance.
red_flags: Automated threats of immediate arrest or police dispatch
Demands for non-standard payment instruments (gift cards, prepaid cards, crypto)
High-pressure urgency designed to prevent rational verification
Caller ID spoofing mimicking official tax or judicial agency phone numbers
source_citation: OECD Task Force on Tax Crimes and Other Crimes / National Tax Agency Warnings
legit_contrast: Government tax and legal authorities communicate formal assessments via secure postal mail or official authenticated digital portals, and never demand immediate payment over phone/SMS via gift cards.

pattern_description: Victims are recruited via messaging apps for simple remote work tasks (boosting ratings, optimizing hotel listings, watching videos), initially receiving small payouts to build trust, before being forced to deposit personal funds into 'composite tasks' to unlock higher commissions.
example_text: Earn $200–$500 daily doing simple app optimization tasks from home. Complete our training module on Telegram and deposit $100 to activate your VIP merchant account level.
red_flags: Unrealistically high daily compensation for minimal, unskilled digital labor
Requirement to deposit personal capital to 'unlock' earnings or clear negative account balances
Operations routed entirely through unverified messaging channels (Telegram, WhatsApp groups)
Absence of official employment contracts or corporate identity verification
source_citation: Global Anti-Fraud Consortium & Transnational Cyber Taskforce Reports
legit_contrast: Legitimate companies pay employees for services rendered; they never demand that workers pay money out of pocket to unlock earned wages or commissions.

pattern_description: Sophisticated real-time phishing proxies intercept banking sessions or enterprise single sign-on (SSO) portals, capturing user credentials and dynamic 2FA time-based tokens instantaneously to compromise accounts.
example_text: Your corporate Microsoft 365 session has expired. Sign in securely to re-authenticate and sync your profile: https://login-microsoftonline.com-auth.net/verify
red_flags: Typosquatted domain names mimicking prominent corporate or cloud authentication pages
Unexpected prompts to re-authenticate credentials outside standard workflow cycles
Absence of standard enterprise Zero-Trust hardware security key or biometric prompts
Dynamic proxy redirects attempting to capture real-time OTP tokens
source_citation: CISA / ENISA Joint Advisory on Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass and Phishing Proxies
legit_contrast: Authorized corporate domains utilize strict enterprise identity providers (IdPs) mapped to internal corporate roots, avoiding ambiguous external hosting paths.
